app.title: HIV trends and treatment access
app.summary: A person picks which countries and which span of years to look at in a sidebar. They then choose one indicator and read its trend over time for each selected country, with a table that keeps the source labels and uncertainty limits. Further tabs set out a fixed-year treatment cascade and the estimated treatment gap by country, compare the estimates from several model specifications and leave-one-country-out runs, and plot coverage against national income. The person can download the cascade table, the model results, the filtered data, or the result of a fixed read-only SQL example as CSV.

task.text: Compare national surveillance estimates across countries over time, and check how sensitive an exploratory association is to the choice of model specification.

data.text: A panel of modelled national estimates (counts, percentages and their published lower and upper limits) by country and year. Censored values keep their original source text, and the panel is joined to economic covariates. Precomputed model-result tables come with it.

stage.text: comparing countries and model specifications after a descriptive panel analysis, before writing it up

mechanism.text: A sidebar country multi-select and year-range slider filter the panel used by the trend tab and the data-explorer tab. Each remaining tab is a fixed summary view (grouped bars, a coefficient table with a chosen specification shown as a metric, a log-axis scatter), and each tab has a CSV download.

field.text: descriptive trends and fixed-effects panel models of national surveillance estimates in epidemiology

workflow.name: compare units' indicators over time and across model specifications, then export the tables

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: The sidebar multi-selects countries and a slider restricts the years; this filters the trend and data-explorer tabs.
An indicator dropdown redraws a line chart with one line per country, above a table of the values, their source text and their lower and upper limits.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: For a fixed year, the cascade tab shows each stage as a percentage with its own denominator, all-population coverage as grouped bars, and the approximate untreated count computed as population × (1 − coverage).
A dropdown picks one model specification and shows its coefficient, interval and sample; a table lists all specifications next to the leave-one-country-out runs.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A log-x scatter of income per capita against coverage for one year, with countries labelled and shown on hover.
Download buttons save the cascade, the model results, the filtered panel, or the output of a fixed read-only SQL example as CSV.

distinctive: censored values (< and > bounds) stay as gaps in the numeric fields while their source text is shown and exported alongside
each cascade stage uses a different denominator, and the page states the population-level equivalents of the target

the same association is shown under many specifications (lags, year effects, covariate, period, denominator, threshold substitution) and with one country left out at a time, to read how sensitive it is
fixed read-only SQL examples run against a bundled database, so a person can check the dashboard numbers against the stored tables

parts.title: Trend filters
parts.summary: Sidebar where the person picks countries and a year range for the trend and data-explorer tabs.

parts.title: Trends
parts.summary: Line chart of one chosen indicator per country over the filtered years, with a table of values, source labels and limits, plus headline metrics.

parts.title: Treatment cascade
parts.summary: Table of the cascade stages for each country, grouped bars of all-population coverage, a bar chart of the estimated untreated count, and a CSV download.

parts.title: Model comparisons
parts.summary: Picks one model specification to show its coefficient and interval, and lists all specifications and the leave-one-country-out runs with their limitations, with a CSV download.

parts.title: GDP comparison
parts.summary: Scatter of income per capita (log axis) against treatment coverage for one year, with countries labelled.

parts.title: Data explorer
parts.summary: Shows the filtered panel as a table to download, and runs fixed read-only SQL examples against the bundled database, with their results also downloadable.
